verdict.rationale: OpenCode's IDE docs name VS Code and Cursor and otherwise say it works in 'any IDE that supports a terminal.' Running it in a JetBrains terminal relies on the host IDE's terminal, not a product capability. Nothing in the evidence documents a JetBrains plugin, interactive diff viewing, or sharing a selected code range as context inside JetBrains; the file-reference shortcut belongs to the documented VS Code/Cursor extension.

support.subject: As a developer, I can view interactive diffs and share selected code as context from within my JetBrains IDE
